When dist_coordinator is non-null, detectOrphans() and isOrphaned() query it directly instead of (or in addition to) the per-call CrossShardTransactionCoordinator. config Orphan-detection configuration. dist_coordinator Wired DistributedCoordinator; may be nullptr.

#### `size_t cleanPercolatorLocks(const std::shared_ptr< themisdb::sharding::CrossShardTransactionCoordinator > &coordinator)`
- Source: `include/sharding/orphan_detector.h`:95
- Brief: Clean Percolator Locks.
- Parameters:
  - `coordinator` (const std::shared_ptr< themisdb::sharding::CrossShardTransactionCoordinator > &): Input parameter.
- Return: Number of stale Percolator locks reclaimed.
- Details: Reclaim stale Percolator locks left by failed coordinators. Scans all active transactions in coordinator, identifies those using the PERCOLATOR protocol whose locks have been held longer than Config::timeout_seconds, and aborts them via the coordinator's abort() method. The abort triggers lock release on every shard participant. coordinator The cross-shard coordinator to scan and clean. Number of stale Percolator locks reclaimed. coordinator Input parameter. Return value. Calls: spdlog::warn(), getActiveTransactions(), std::chrono::system_clock::now(), std::chrono::seconds(), spdlog::info(), count(), abort().

#### `RecoveryAction getRecoveryAction(ShardingErrorCode ec) noexcept`
- Source: `include/sharding/sharding_error_recovery_impl.h`:98
- Brief: Get the recovery action for a given error code.
- Parameters:
  - `ec` (ShardingErrorCode): The error code.
- Return: Recovery action to be taken.
- Details: This function is the canonical source of truth for error recovery. All sharding components MUST use this to determine how to handle errors. ec The error code. Recovery action to be taken. Recovery strategies are deterministic and stateless (always return the same action for the same input). Mapping rationale: QUORUM_LOST (1) Strategy: FAIL_CLOSED Rationale: Cannot proceed without quorum; no safe fallback. Recovery: Operator must restore node availability. Details: See QUORUM_LOSS_RUNBOOK.md COORDINATOR_FAILURE (2) Strategy: DEGRADE_READONLY Rationale: Coordinator is essential for writes but not reads. Recovery: Automatic failover to replica or manual restart. Details: Existing writes in-flight may remain in IN_DOUBT state. SHARD_UNAVAILABLE (3) Strategy: RETRY_WITH_BACKOFF Rationale: Transient network partition or temporary unavailability. Recovery: Automatic retry; may succeed when shard recovers. Details: Max 5 attempts with exponential backoff (100ms → 10s). MIGRATION_CONFLICT (4) Strategy: FAIL_CLOSED Rationale: Concurrent migrations to same shard must be serialized. Recovery: Caller must wait for in-flight migration and retry. Details: Lock-based serialization prevents this in normal operation. WAL_CORRUPTION (5) Strategy: RECOVERY_REQUIRED Rationale: Data integrity compromised; manual inspection needed. Recovery: Operator must inspect/repair WAL before resuming. Details: Automatic recovery is unsafe (data loss risk). CONSENSUS_TIMEOUT (6) Strategy: TIMEOUT_AND_ABORT Rationale: Operation timed out; abort to unblock client. Recovery: Client may retry; consensus layer may eventually succeed. Details: Bounded timeout prevents indefinite hangs. TRANSACTION_IN_DOUBT (7) Strategy: TIMEOUT_AND_ABORT Rationale: 2PC coordinator crashed; must await recovery. Recovery: Automatic coordinator recovery resolves in-doubt txns. Details: Participant blocks conflicting writes until resolved. ROUTING_RING_INVALID (8) Strategy: FAIL_CLOSED Rationale: Routing configuration is corrupted; cannot proceed safely. Recovery: Operator must repair topology/shard configuration. Details: Automatic fallback would mask consistency issues. MIGRATION_FAULT (9) Strategy: ROLLBACK_AUTOMATIC Rationale: Partial migration; must revert to safe state. Recovery: Automatic rollback restores previous shard assignment. Details: Rollback is idempotent (can be replayed safely). RING_EMPTY (10) Strategy: FAIL_CLOSED Rationale: No shards available; cannot route any request. Recovery: Operator must add shards to cluster. Details: Automatic degradation would route to nowhere. SHARD_INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE (11) Strategy: FAIL_CLOSED Rationale: Configuration error (shard index > kMaxShards). Recovery: Operator must correct shard index. Details: Automatic fallback would hide configuration bugs. INTERNAL_ERROR (12) Strategy: RECOVERY_REQUIRED Rationale: Unclassified internal error; nature unknown. Recovery: Operator must inspect logs and diagnose. Details: Automatic handling unsafe without understanding error.

#### `std::string routeByDomain(themis::distributed_knowledge::AdapterDomainType domain) const`
- Source: `include/sharding/adaptive_shard_router.h`:228
- Brief: n/a
- Parameters:
  - `domain` (themis::distributed_knowledge::AdapterDomainType): Domain type to look up
- Return: shard_id of the best-scoring shard, or "" if no score exists
- Details: Route a query to the shard with the highest accuracy_delta for the given adapter domain. When two shards share the same best accuracy_delta the one with the lower pending_llm_requests (LEAST_LOADED) wins. Fallback: if no shard has registered a score for domain, the method returns an empty string and callers should use the default route() behaviour. Load tie-break semantics: Fresh queue snapshots win over stale/missing snapshots. For equally fresh snapshots with equal score, lower pending queue wins. Remaining ties are resolved deterministically by lexical shard_id order. domain Domain type to look up shard_id of the best-scoring shard, or "" if no score exists

#### `LiveMigrationResult liveMigrate(const std::string &source_shard_id, const std::string &target_shard_id, uint64_t token_range_start, uint64_t token_range_end, std::shared_ptr< ShardTopology > topology=nullptr, std::shared_ptr< WALShipper > wal_shipper=nullptr, const LiveMigrationConfig &live_cfg=LiveMigrationConfig{}, ProgressCallback progress_callback=nullptr)`
- Source: `include/sharding/data_migrator.h`:215
- Brief: ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── Live migration (dual-write protocol) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
- Parameters:
  - `source_shard_id` (const std::string &): Identifier of the source shard.
  - `target_shard_id` (const std::string &): Identifier of the target shard.
  - `token_range_start` (uint64_t): Input parameter.
  - `token_range_end` (uint64_t): Input parameter.
  - `topology` (std::shared_ptr< ShardTopology >): Input parameter.
  - `wal_shipper` (std::shared_ptr< WALShipper >): Input parameter.
  - `live_cfg` (const LiveMigrationConfig &): Input parameter.
  - `progress_callback` (ProgressCallback): Input parameter.
- Return: LiveMigrationResult
- Details: Perform a live (dual-write) migration with zero read-unavailability. Protocol: Bulk-copy existing data from source to target using migrate(). While the copy runs the source shard continues accepting writes. After the bulk copy the target shard is registered with wal_shipper so it receives incremental WAL entries for the migrated token range. Once the WAL lag drops below live_cfg.max_wal_lag_bytes an atomic cutover is performed: topology is updated via ShardTopology, the source shard becomes read-only for the token range, and the target shard becomes authoritative. source_shard_id Source (hot) shard target_shard_id Destination shard for the token range token_range_start Start of token range to migrate token_range_end End of token range to migrate topology ShardTopology for atomic cutover (may be nullptr to skip cutover) wal_shipper WALShipper for incremental catchup (may be nullptr to skip WAL phase) live_cfg Live migration configuration progress_callback Optional progress callback for bulk-copy phase LiveMigrationResult source_shard_id Identifier of the source shard. target_shard_id Identifier of the target shard. token_range_start Input parameter. token_range_end Input parameter. topology Input parameter. wal_shipper Input parameter. live_cfg Input parameter. progress_callback Input parameter. Return value. Calls: generateMigrationId(), migrate(), verifyIntegrity(), addReplica(), std::chrono::steady_clock::now(), getReplicaInfo(), getStatistics(), std::this_thread::sleep_for().

#### `bool percolatorCommit(DistributedTransaction &txn)`
- Source: `include/sharding/distributed_transaction.h`:436
- Brief: Percolator-style commit for SNAPSHOT_ISOLATION transactions.
- Parameters:
  - `txn` (DistributedTransaction &): Input/output parameter.
- Return: True if all participants prepared and committed successfully.
- Details: ------------------------------------------------------------------------ Percolator-style commit path (used for SNAPSHOT_ISOLATION transactions) ------------------------------------------------------------------------ Executes cross-shard conflict detection and TrueTime-anchored commit for snapshot-isolated transactions. The full sequence is: Prepare phase — all participants vote COMMIT or ABORT (conflict check). Any ABORT vote triggers abort of all prepared participants and returns false. Derive commit timestamp via TrueTime::now_with_uncertainty().latest. Perform commit-wait: spin until TT.now().earliest > commit_ts. Send COMMIT to all participants with the agreed timestamp. This path is chosen when Config::use_percolator_for_snapshot == true and the transaction's isolation_level == SNAPSHOT_ISOLATION. txn Distributed transaction (state mutated in-place). True if all participants prepared and committed successfully. txn Input/output parameter. True when the operation succeeds. Calls: preparePhase(), THEMIS_WARN(), sendAbort(), now_with_uncertainty(), THEMIS_DEBUG(), count(), waitUntil(), emplace_back().

#### `EpochToken bumpEpoch(const std::string &reason)`
- Source: `include/sharding/epoch_fencing.h`:304
- Brief: Atomically increment the epoch and return a fresh token.
- Parameters:
  - `reason` (const std::string &): Input parameter.
- Return: New EpochToken with epoch == currentEpoch().
- Details: Bump Epoch. Only the elected leader should call this. On epoch bump all in-flight tokens from the previous epoch become stale immediately. reason Log message describing why the epoch was bumped. New EpochToken with epoch == currentEpoch(). Virtual to enable test doubles that return controlled epoch values (e.g. epoch=0 to exercise the invalid-epoch guard in failover paths). reason Input parameter. Return value. Calls: fetch_add(), lk(), spdlog::info(), std::chrono::system_clock::now().

#### `FencingResult checkToken(const EpochToken &token, const NodeId &source_node)`
- Source: `include/sharding/epoch_fencing.h`:333
- Brief: Check whether token authorises a write in the current epoch.
- Parameters:
  - `token` (const EpochToken &): Input parameter.
  - `source_node` (const NodeId &): Input parameter.
- Return: Return value.
- Details: Check Token. ALLOWED → proceed with the write STALE_EPOCH → reject; if auto_stonith the STONITH call may follow INVALID_TOKEN → reject; structurally invalid token STONITH_ISSUED → stale token AND STONITH successfully issued STONITH_FAILED → stale token AND STONITH failed token Token attached to the incoming write RPC. source_node Node that sent the request (for STONITH targeting). token Input parameter. source_node Input parameter. Return value. Calls: spdlog::warn(), load(), lk(), issueStonith().

#### `void setRaftMembershipGateFn(RaftMembershipGateFn fn)`
- Source: `include/sharding/gossip_protocol.h`:326
- Brief: Register a Raft membership gate for gossip-driven topology mutations (CC-4).
- Parameters:
  - `fn` (RaftMembershipGateFn): Input parameter.
- Details: Set Raft Membership Gate Fn. When a gate function is registered, any gossip-discovered peer that is NOT yet in the ShardTopology is admitted only if the gate returns true. A peer rejected by the gate is still tracked in the internal peers_ map so that it participates in health-monitoring rounds, but it is NEVER written to the routing topology and NEVER influences quorum calculations. When no gate is registered (the default), gossip-discovered peers are added to the topology with a one-time warning — preserving backward compatibility while clearly marking the unprotected path. fn Gate function. Pass nullptr to remove a previously registered gate and revert to the legacy warn+add behaviour. Thread-safety: the function pointer is stored under peers_mutex_. fn Input parameter. Calls: lock(), std::move().

#### `void onCertificateRotated()`
- Source: `include/sharding/mtls_connection_pool.h`:318
- Brief: Graceful connection drain triggered by a certificate rotation event.
- Parameters: none
- Details: On Certificate Rotated. Closes all idle connections immediately (they will be re-established with the new certificate on the next request). In-flight connections are allowed to complete; each endpoint pool stops issuing new connections from its current TLS context until the drain completes. This method is non-blocking: it schedules the drain and returns. Callers that need to await completion should poll getStatistics() or wait for the idle-connection count to return to its expected level. Wire-up: call this from the PKI client's certificate-rotation callback so that stale TLS sessions are not reused after a cert rotation. Calls: lock(), size(), closeAll().

#### `bool compact(const LSN &up_to_lsn, const std::string &node_id)`
- Source: `include/sharding/paxos_wal.h`:218
- Brief: Compact (truncate) the WAL at the next segment boundary before up_to_lsn.
- Parameters:
  - `up_to_lsn` (const LSN &): Input parameter.
  - `node_id` (const std::string &): Identifier of the node.
- Return: true on success
- Details: Compact. Called after a Paxos snapshot has been successfully persisted. WAL entries are discarded on a segment-granularity basis: all segments whose segment number is strictly less than up_to_lsn.segment are deleted by WALManager::truncate(). The oldest retained data is therefore the beginning of the segment that contains up_to_lsn, not necessarily the exact record at up_to_lsn. Callers should pass the LSN of the last committed entry in the snapshot so that recovery can always start from a valid segment boundary. The operation first writes a SNAPSHOT marker WAL entry so that a reader replaying from an older checkpoint can detect the compaction boundary. up_to_lsn LSN whose preceding segments will be discarded node_id Node performing the compaction (used in the marker) true on success up_to_lsn Input parameter. node_id Identifier of the node. True when the operation succeeds. Calls: lock(), spdlog::error(), toString(), std::chrono::system_clock::now(), time_since_epoch(), count(), createEntry(), append().

- Source: `include/sharding/prometheus_metrics.h`:115
- Brief: Increment the canonical cross-shard request counter.

  - `outcome` (const std::string &): Input parameter.
- Details: Record Cross Shard Request. Emits the Prometheus counter sharding_cross_shard_requests_total with labels {shard_id, operation, outcome}. This counter is the Phase C observability gate required by the sharding module roadmap. shard_id Target shard identifier ("shard-0", "shard-7", …). operation Logical operation: "route", "scatter_gather", "prepare", "commit", "abort", "repair", "anti_entropy". outcome "success", "error", or "timeout". Call this for every cross-shard RPC dispatch point, not just joins. For join-specific metrics use recordCrossShardJoin(). shard_id Identifier of the shard. operation Input parameter. outcome Input parameter.

#### `Result postBinary(const ShardInfo &shard_info, const std::string &path, const uint8_t *data, std::size_t size)`
- Source: `include/sharding/remote_executor.h`:143
- Brief: Post Binary.
- Parameters:
  - `shard_info` (const ShardInfo &): Input parameter.
  - `path` (const std::string &): Input parameter.
  - `data` (const uint8_t *): Input parameter.
  - `size` (std::size_t): Input parameter.
- Return: Result with success flag, shard_id, and optional error message.
- Details: Transfer a raw binary payload to a remote shard via HTTP POST. Intended for KV-state transfer (Phase 5 KV-Prefix Cross-Shard sharing): the serialised KV cache for a shared system-prompt prefix is POSTed to the target shard so that it can warm its local KV cache and reduce time-to-first-token (TTFT) for requests that share the same prefix. Content-Type is set to "application/octet-stream". The response body is returned in Result::response (base64-encoded by the mTLS layer if non-printable characters are present). shard_info Target shard. path Request path (e.g., "/api/v1/kv-prefix/ingest"). data Pointer to binary payload bytes. size Payload size in bytes. Result with success flag, shard_id, and optional error message. shard_info Input parameter. path Input parameter. data Input parameter. size Input parameter. Return value. Calls: reserve(), std::move(), post().

- Source: `include/sharding/shard_rpc_server.h`:110
- Brief: Collect all active local wait-for edges for distributed deadlock detection.
- Parameters: none
- Details: The coordinator calls this on every shard during each deadlock-detection cycle to build a cluster-wide wait-for graph. Each entry in the returned vector represents a directed edge: waiting_transaction_id is blocked by blocking_transaction_id on this shard. Default implementation returns an empty list (no local lock waits known). Override in shards that maintain a local lock-wait state.

#### `themis::Result< std::string > runConsistencyCheck() const`
- Source: `include/sharding/shard_repair_engine.h`:292
- Brief: Run a synchronous replica consistency check across all shards.
- Parameters: none
- Return: Ok<std::string> with the summary message.
- Details: Iterates the last-known per-shard health reports (populated by the background scan loop or the most recent triggerFullScan() call) and returns a human-readable summary string. The summary format is: "Replica validation OK: <n> shard(s) healthy" — all healthy "Replica validation: <n> degraded / <m> unrecoverable shard(s) found" — issues found This method is intentionally lightweight and non-blocking: it reads cached state rather than triggering a new network scan. Use triggerFullScan() before calling this if fresh data is required. Designed to be passed as the check_fn of a ReplicaValidationHandler registered with the DatabaseMaintenanceOrchestrator: autohandler=std::make_shared<ReplicaValidationHandler>( [engine](){returnengine->runConsistencyCheck();}); orchestrator.registerTaskHandler( MaintenanceTaskType::REPLICA_VALIDATION, std::move(handler)); Ok<std::string> with the summary message. Err<Error> if reports indicate unrecoverable shard(s) (ErrorCode::ERR_STORAGE_TRANSACTION_FAILED).

  - `max_key` (const std::string &): Upper bound of the key range (inclusive)
- Return: Ordered list of unique shard identifiers
- Details: Return all shards that may hold keys in [min_key, max_key]. Traverses the consistent-hash ring clockwise from the virtual node responsible for min_key to the one responsible for max_key and collects every unique shard encountered. When min and max map to the same shard, a single-element vector is returned. When no nodes are registered an empty vector is returned. collection Collection name min_key Lower bound of the key range (inclusive) max_key Upper bound of the key range (inclusive) Ordered list of unique shard identifiers

#### `TwoPhaseCommitParticipant(const std::string &shard_id, ValidateAndLockCallback validate=nullptr, ApplyOperationsCallback apply=nullptr, ReleaseLockCallback release=nullptr)`
- Source: `include/sharding/two_phase_commit_participant.h`:130
- Brief: Construct a participant with optional storage callbacks.

Any exception thrown by WALManager::append() or WALManager::flush() is caught and logged as an error using component_label and component_id so callers see a consistent diagnostic message without crashing. The returned LSN can be used by callers that need to emit additional success diagnostics; std::nullopt indicates that nothing was persisted because the WAL was disabled or a write failed. wal Target WAL manager (may be nullptr). type Logical operation type. txn_id Transaction identifier. data Additional JSON payload. sync When true, call wal->flush() after append. component_label Human-readable role label, e.g. "coordinator" or "participant". Used in the error log message. component_id Instance identifier, e.g. coordinator_id_ or shard_id_. Used in the error log message. Assigned LSN on success; std::nullopt on noop/failure.

#### `std::vector< FKViolation > validate(const std::string &transaction_id, const std::map< std::string, std::vector< std::string > > &shard_operations) const`
- Source: `include/sharding/cross_shard_fk_validator.h`:288
- Brief: Validate FK constraints for a pending transaction.
- Parameters:
  - `transaction_id` (const std::string &): Global transaction ID (used in log messages).
  - `shard_operations` (const std::map< std::string, std::vector< std::string > > &): Map of shard_id → list of serialised operations.
- Return: List of FK violations; empty on full compliance.
- Details: Parses the per-shard operation lists, extracts INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE ops, and evaluates every registered FK constraint. Non-deferrable violations must be treated as prepare failures by the caller. Operation JSON format Each string in shard_operations must be a JSON object with at least: {"op":"INSERT"\|"UPDATE"\|"DELETE", "table":"<table>", //ForINSERT/UPDATEonachildtable: "data":{"<fk_column>":"<value>",...}, //ForDELETEonaparenttable: "key":"<pk_value>" } Operations in unknown tables or with unrelated columns are silently skipped. transaction_id Global transaction ID (used in log messages). shard_operations Map of shard_id → list of serialised operations. List of FK violations; empty on full compliance. Deferrable-constraint violations are included in the returned list but flagged with FKViolation::deferrable = true so the coordinator can decide whether to abort or proceed.

Implements the Calvin deterministic database protocol: Phase 1 (Sequencing): Assign a deterministic global sequence number Phase 2 (Lock Acquisition): Pre-acquire all locks in a canonical order Phase 3 (Execution): Execute and commit in the pre-determined order Unlike 2PC, Calvin does not require a voting round; all participants execute the same pre-ordered transaction log, guaranteeing determinism. txn Input/output parameter. #### `void setDeferredPreCommitCallback(DeferredPreCommitFn fn)`
- Source: `include/sharding/cross_shard_transaction.h`:571
- Brief: Set callback for deferred PreCommit retry (3PC non-blocking mode).
- Parameters:
  - `fn` (DeferredPreCommitFn): Input parameter.
- Details: Set Deferred Pre Commit Callback. When set, failed PreCommit operations do not immediately abort the transaction. Instead, execute3PC() hands the failed shard list to this callback for deferred retry orchestration. Exception safety / contract: The callback must not throw. If it throws, execute3PC() treats this as a fatal orchestration failure and fails closed (abort path) instead of silently downgrading behavior. fn Callable void(txn_id, failed_shards) that schedules retry handling for failed PreCommit participants; must not throw. fn Input parameter. Calls: lock(), std::move().

#### `void setForeignKeyValidator(std::shared_ptr< CrossShardForeignKeyValidator > validator)`
- Source: `include/sharding/cross_shard_transaction.h`:593
- Brief: Inject a cross-shard foreign-key validator (issue #5392).
- Parameters:
  - `validator` (std::shared_ptr< CrossShardForeignKeyValidator >): Input parameter.
- Details: Set Foreign Key Validator. When a non-null validator is set, prepare() invokes CrossShardForeignKeyValidator::validate() before dispatching the prepare RPCs to participants. Any non-deferrable FK violation causes prepare() to return false (transaction aborted). Passing nullptr removes a previously installed validator. The coordinator takes shared ownership of the validator so it can be shared across coordinator instances in tests. Thread safety The method is protected by the callbacks_mutex_ and is safe to call concurrently with ongoing transactions; the validator pointer is snapshotted at the start of each prepare() call. validator Fully configured CrossShardForeignKeyValidator, or nullptr to disable cross-shard FK checking. validator Input parameter.

#### `bool execute(CrossShardTransaction &txn, SendPrepareFn prepare_fn, SendCommitFn commit_fn, SendAbortFn abort_fn)`
- Source: `include/sharding/cross_shard_transaction.h`:909
- Brief: Execute the Percolator protocol for txn.
- Parameters:
  - `txn` (CrossShardTransaction &): Input/output parameter.
  - `prepare_fn` (SendPrepareFn): Input parameter.
  - `commit_fn` (SendCommitFn): Input parameter.
  - `abort_fn` (SendAbortFn): Input parameter.
- Return: true if the transaction committed successfully.
- Details: Execute. Drives the full Percolator commit sequence: Phase 1 – PreWrite: lock secondaries first, then lock primary. Phase 2 – Assign TrueTime commit timestamp, perform commit-wait. Phase 3 – Commit primary, then commit secondaries (lock release). The shard-level operations are performed via the supplied callbacks so this class is independent of the RPC transport layer and can be used without a live CrossShardTransactionCoordinator. txn Transaction to commit (state is mutated in-place). prepare_fn Callback: lock (prepare) one shard. commit_fn Callback: commit one shard. abort_fn Callback: abort / unlock one shard. true if the transaction committed successfully. txn Input/output parameter. prepare_fn Input parameter. commit_fn Input parameter. abort_fn Input parameter. True when the operation succeeds. Calls: spdlog::info(), empty(), spdlog::error(), std::min(), std::chrono::milliseconds(), spdlog::debug(), count(), std::this_thread::sleep_for().

#### `themis::Result< std::string > runConsistencyCheck() const`
- Source: `include/sharding/shard_repair_engine.h`:292
- Brief: Run a synchronous replica consistency check across all shards.
- Parameters: none
- Return: Ok<std::string> with the summary message.
- Details: Iterates the last-known per-shard health reports (populated by the background scan loop or the most recent triggerFullScan() call) and returns a human-readable summary string. The summary format is: "Replica validation OK: <n> shard(s) healthy" — all healthy "Replica validation: <n> degraded / <m> unrecoverable shard(s) found" — issues found This method is intentionally lightweight and non-blocking: it reads cached state rather than triggering a new network scan. Use triggerFullScan() before calling this if fresh data is required. Designed to be passed as the check_fn of a ReplicaValidationHandler registered with the DatabaseMaintenanceOrchestrator: autohandler=std::make_shared<ReplicaValidationHandler>( [engine](){returnengine->runConsistencyCheck();}); orchestrator.registerTaskHandler( MaintenanceTaskType::REPLICA_VALIDATION, std::move(handler)); Ok<std::string> with the summary message. Err<Error> if reports indicate unrecoverable shard(s) (ErrorCode::ERR_STORAGE_TRANSACTION_FAILED).
